extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX Coordinators, campus compliance officers, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX compliance for postsecondary institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble to final Department of Education Title IX regulations describing requirements for confidential employees, the public awareness event exception, evidentiary and advisor rules, and the duties/responsibilities of a Title IX Coordinator at postsecondary institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee explanation of confidential status (§106.44(d)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain their status as confidential for purposes of this part, including the circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department replaced the proposed, more cursory explanation with this more detailed requirement to ensure individuals understand when confidentiality will apply and when it may not. This requirement applies to all three categories of confidential employees. Organizational edits were made for clarity; the rule aims to enable informed confidential reporting while protecting reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee must provide Title IX contact and complaint guidance (§106.44(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain how to contact the recipient's Title IX Coordinator and how to make a complaint of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(d)(2)(ii) requires that confidential employees provide sufficient guidance to enable the student (or other reporting person) to report to the Title IX Coordinator, including contact information and instructions on making a complaint. The Department sees benefits in confidential employees giving this information to empower reporting without eliminating confidential reporting options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee must explain Title IX Coordinator's roles and supportive measures (§106.44(d)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee must explain that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures, initiate an informal resolution process, or initiate an investigation under the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement helps counter misconceptions that the only action a Title IX Coordinator can take is to initiate an investigation and assists complainants in considering options. Confidential employees may also provide additional information about supportive measures; certain confidential employees (e.g., mental health counselors) may be involved in implementing supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability to researchers who are confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of §106.44(d)(2) apply to researchers who qualify as confidential employees under the third category of the definition, but the Department declines to specifically require researchers to include this information as part of their informed consent process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to mandate that researchers include the §106.44(d)(2) information in consent forms so as not to inappropriately interfere with researchers' independence and professional judgment, but nothing prohibits researchers from providing the information. Confidential-employee obligations still apply where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees and minor children — flexibility and compliance with other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department acknowledges special considerations for confidential employees assisting minor children in elementary and secondary school contexts but declines to add further requirements, emphasizing importance of flexibility and discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in §106.44(d)(2) exempts confidential employees from complying with other Federal, State, or local mandatory reporting laws. Consistent with §106.6(g), the provision does not derogate legal rights of parents/guardians to act on behalf of minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of evidence from confidential employees unless confidentiality is waived (§106.45(b)(7)(i) revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must exclude evidence provided to a confidential employee from an investigation unless the person to whom the confidentiality is owed has voluntarily waived that confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects information shared with confidential employees from being used in investigations without the disclosing person's consent, helping preserve trust in confidential resources and encouraging reporting. The Department revised the proposed language in response to commenters to incorporate this protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employees not required to act as advisors; restrictions on appointment as advisor (§106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees are not required to serve as advisors during grievance procedures. A postsecondary institution may not appoint a current confidential employee (or someone who received information as a confidential employee) to serve as the advisor to ask questions on behalf of a party when the institution is required to appoint such an advisor for a live hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a party may choose a confidential employee as their advisor of choice (§106.46(e)(2)), institutions must not appoint confidential employees in instances where they are required to appoint an advisor to ask questions—this avoids conflicts of interest and protects legal privileges related to confidential communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public awareness event exception scope (§106.44(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The public awareness event exception applies only to a public event held on a postsecondary institution's campus or through an online platform sponsored by the institution to raise awareness about sex-based harassment, and only to information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception is intentionally limited to on-campus or institution-sponsored online awareness events (e.g., Take Back the Night) and to sex-based harassment (not broader potential sex discrimination). It does not cover off-campus community events, disclosures made in academic assignments, or social media. The Department declined to further define 'public event' or 'sponsored' but removed limiting language that implied the event must be associated with the institution's education program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to report public awareness event disclosures to Title IX Coordinator and use information for prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Information disclosed at a public awareness event must be provided to the Title IX Coordinator (employee notification requirements), and the postsecondary institution must use the information to inform its efforts to prevent sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the exception limits certain required responses, the institution must still report information to the Title IX Coordinator, who will determine whether it indicates an imminent and serious threat and coordinate preventive measures (examples given: increasing lighting, offering transportation options after dark). Institutions may also post contact information or information about how disclosures will be used, but the Department declines to mandate specific content at events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imminent and serious threat threshold for public awareness event disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Even under the public awareness event exception, a postsecondary institution must respond to notifications of information that indicates an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant, any students, employees, or other persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a threat is indicated, the Title IX Coordinator must comply with obligations under §106.44(f), including conducting a fact-specific analysis under §106.44(f)(1)(v) to determine whether the Title IX Coordinator must initiate a formal complaint under the institution's grievance procedures. The Department changed 'immediate and serious threat' to 'imminent and serious threat' to align with §106.44(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator role and three-part structure (§106.44(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(f) clarifies that (1) the Title IX Coordinator is responsible for coordinating a recipient's compliance with Title IX and this part; (2) paragraphs §106.44(f)(1)(i)-(vii) describe actions the Title IX Coordinator must take upon notification of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination to promptly and effectively end discrimination, prevent recurrence, and remedy effects; and (3) §106.44(f)(2) allows the Title IX Coordinator to refrain from those specific actions if they reasonably determine the conduct could not constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reorganized the Coordinator requirements to align with the overall compliance framework and clarify when actions are required. The Department determined that the Coordinator must take the specified actions in (f)(1)(i)-(vii) to meet Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate, but retained a reasonableness-based exception under (f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected substantive actions of Title IX Coordinator (early intervention, equitable treatment, supportive measures, prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Title IX Coordinator must coordinate early intervention efforts in response to possible sex discrimination; provide consistent, equitable treatment and support to individuals impacted by sex discrimination, including offering supportive measures; offer resources to end sex discrimination and prevent its recurrence; and respond to patterns, trends, and risk factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department states these requirements will help recipients provide an educational environment free from sex discrimination, giving coordinators guidance and flexibility beyond the 2020 amendments. These actions include oversight of responses to individual reports and institution-wide prevention efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient remains ultimately responsible; Coordinator coordinates compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although §106.44(f) assigns duties to the Title IX Coordinator, the recipient (institution) remains responsible for compliance with Title IX and the implementing regulations; the Title IX Coordinator's role is to coordinate the recipient's obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added language clarifying that the Title IX Coordinator coordinates the recipient's compliance to emphasize institutional accountability while preserving the Coordinator's oversight and trusted-resource role. The Department will hold the recipient responsible for meeting obligations under the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to delegate Title IX Coordinator duties and use of designees
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may designate more than one employee to serve as a Title IX Coordinator and may delegate specific duties of the Title IX Coordinator to one or more designees; however, the Title IX Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight for offering and coordinating supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(a) permits multiple designees and delegation of duties, which allows institutions flexibility in implementation; the final regulations do not restrict how duties to offer and coordinate supportive measures may be delegated, but ultimate oversight remains with the Title IX Coordinator.
